events.text: Dosu the tracker squats over a print in the frost as wide as a cart wheel. "Five toes," he says, "and it walked here on purpose, where we would see it." Above the pass, a long white shape lies along a ledge and watches the two of you come up the mountain. It does not hide. The White Tiger never hides.

effects.log: You climb all afternoon. When you reach the ledge it has moved to the next one, and is still watching.

choices.text: Make camp where it can see you

effects.log: You build a small fire in the open. All night two green lamps hang in the dark above it.
"To see if you are worth the climb," he says. "Most are not."

events.text: In the village below the cliffs a magistrate's clerk has been found tied to a pine, unharmed, with his false ledgers pinned to his chest. The villagers whisper of a horned beast with a mane like a lion's that walks in at night and sorts the honest from the crooked. A Haechi has come down from the mountain, and it is looking at everyone.

effects.log: You stand in the square at dusk with nothing in your hands. Something large breathes behind the shrine wall, and decides.
The clerk thanks you and runs. Somewhere up the slope, a deep sound like a laugh.

choices.text: Follow its tracks into the hills

effects.log: The tracks lead past every house that cheats its neighbours, and around every house that does not.

events.text: Where the Qilin walks, the grass does not bend. Dosu shows you a meadow full of hoofprints and not one broken stem. "It does not fight," he says. "It does not have to. People who mean it harm simply never find it."

choices.text: Leave your weapons at the meadow's edge

effects.log: You walk in empty-handed. The meadow is very quiet, and you are no longer sure you are alone.
You find nothing. At sunset, when you give up, there is one fresh print beside your boot.
An old herder says it came the year the war ended, and will leave the year the next one begins.

events.text: The fishermen of the black lake will not put out any more. Something lives under the water that is longer than their boats laid end to end, and in the evenings it lifts its head and looks at the sky the way a prisoner looks at a window. An Imugi, a serpent that has waited a thousand years to become a dragon.

effects.log: The water goes still around your boat. Something huge passes under it, slowly, and does not touch it.

choices.text: Sit on the shore and talk to the water

effects.log: You talk about patience, about walls you could not break. The lake listens.

choices.text: Pay the fishermen for their lost season

effects.log: They take the silver and look at you as if you are mad. You probably are.

events.text: A mining town has lost its picks, its pots, its door hinges and the iron bell of its temple, all in one week. The trail of iron filings leads to a cave where something the size of a bull is asleep on a pile of nails, snoring like a bellows. Bulgasari, the iron-eater. It cannot be killed, the stories say. They do not say whether it can be kept.

choices.text: Leave it a gift of scrap iron

effects.log: You drag a sack of broken blades to the cave mouth. In the morning the sack is gone and the snoring is happier.
One eye opens, the colour of a forge. It looks at your sword with great interest.
Picks, hinges, a bell, the town's whole iron. Whoever keeps this beast will need a very large smithy.

events.text: The tracks of the fox go in nine directions at once and come back to where they began. A traveller you meet on the road twice in one day, going the same way both times, smiles at you with very old eyes. The Nine-Tailed Fox is testing you before you have even begun to test it.

effects.log: The traveller laughs, a sound like dry leaves, and is not there. Nine tails flick in the long grass.

choices.text: Keep walking as if you noticed nothing

effects.log: You walk on. Behind you, something curious follows at a distance.

choices.text: Leave out rice wine and a bowl of plums

effects.log: In the morning the plums are gone and the wine is not. The fox, it seems, has opinions.

events.text: Dosu the tracker comes to your gate with mud to his knees. "There is a great one in the high country," he says, "the kind the old houses kept. It has been watching the road for a month. I think it is waiting for someone."

effects.log: He names a price that makes you wince and earns every copper of it.
You go up alone. The mountain is very large, and you are not.
"The {gb_kind}," he says. "I have only ever seen its tracks. That is close enough for most."

events.text: Herders on the steppe border say Gray Mother Ashina has come south, the great gray wolf that ran beside the Khagans' banners for three hundred years. With no Khagan left to run beside, she howls every night from the same hill, and the horses will not graze within sight of it.

choices.text: Ride to the hill at dusk

effects.log: She is there against the red sky, larger than any wolf should be. She does not run. She watches you come.

choices.text: Ask the herders to show you her trail

effects.log: They show you, from a long way off, and will not go a step further.
You turn back. It will still be there. Things that old are very patient.

events.text: Nine-Coil Nammae, the river serpent of the Nine Rivers, has left the delta of the fallen kingdom and swum upriver into the ten provinces. Ferrymen tie offerings of rice cakes to their prows. Where she sleeps the river runs backwards for an hour at dawn.

choices.text: Wait at the ferry crossing at dawn

effects.log: The river slows, stops, and runs backwards. A coil as broad as a road turns over in the brown water.

choices.text: Buy a ferryman's rice cakes and tie them on

effects.log: The cakes are gone before the boat reaches the far bank.
You turn back. It will still be there. Things that old are very patient.

events.text: Old Shiokaze, the sea dragon of the Rising Tide, has been seen off the coast since its empire fell, coiled around an island that was not on any chart last year. The fishing fleets come home early. The sea is very calm, and very watchful.

choices.text: Hire a boat to the new island

effects.log: The boatman takes you as close as he dares. The island breathes.

choices.text: Walk the beach at low tide

effects.log: Scales the size of shields wash up on the sand, cool and blue as deep water.
You turn back. It will still be there. Things that old are very patient.

events.text: Gangkar the White, the snow lion of the plateau, has come down from the passes of the fallen Snow Lion Empire. Monks of the border monastery say it walked three times around their stupa and lay down in the snow outside their gate, as if waiting for a word nobody there knows.

effects.log: The lion lifts its great maned head as you come up the steps, and its breath smokes in the cold.
"If we knew it," the abbot says, "it would not be waiting outside."
You turn back. It will still be there. Things that old are very patient.

events.text: It is over at sundown, on a shelf of broken rock above the clouds. {gb_name} lies with its sides heaving and its eyes on yours, and when you lower your weapon it lowers its head. Not beaten. Satisfied. You have been weighed and found heavy enough.

effects.log: You bow, deeply, to an enemy that has become something else. It watches you do it, and seems to approve.

choices.text: Sit beside it until the stars come out

effects.log: Neither of you moves for a long time. Your breathing slows to match its.
It lets you. Its blood is warm on your hands, and the cuts are already closing.

events.text: You wait through the night in the snow with your hands open on your knees. Near dawn {gb_name} comes out of the dark and lies down beside you, close enough that you feel its warmth through your coat. Neither of you says anything. Neither of you needs to.

effects.log: It allows the hand. Somewhere in its chest a sound starts, low and steady, like a temple bell far off.

choices.text: Keep still until it moves first

effects.log: It moves first, at sunrise: to its feet, and then a few steps toward your house, looking back.

events.text: The {gb_kind} has had enough of you before you have had enough of it. One blow sends you down the scree in a shower of stones, and by the time you have your breath back the slope is empty. Dosu helps you up. "It let you live," he says. "That means it wants you to come back."

effects.log: You will. It knows it, too.

choices.text: Ask Dosu how it can be done

effects.log: "Slower," he says. "Or stronger. Or kinder. Never all three at once."

events.text: You wait in the cold until your fingers stop feeling anything. The {gb_kind} comes close enough once that you hear it breathing, and then it decides something, and goes. The snow fills its prints before the morning.

effects.log: You thaw by a brazier for a week. You dream of green eyes the whole time.
Nothing comes. But you hear it, very far off, answering the wind.

events.text: Gray Mother Ashina stands over you in the long grass with her jaws an inch from your throat, and then, very slowly, she steps back and sits. The steppe is silent. Three hundred years she ran beside the Khagans' banners. Now she looks at you as if trying to remember what a banner is for.

choices.text: Tell her: ours is new, but it will last

effects.log: She listens to the words, then to the voice under them. She stands and walks to your side.

choices.text: Let her decide in her own time

effects.log: She decides by evening. She comes home with you, a long way behind, and never quite out of sight.

events.text: The beast of a fallen empire does not yield easily, and it does not yield to anyone. But it yields to you: an old, proud creature that has lost one house already, choosing a second with its eyes open. The jianghu will talk of this for a generation.

choices.text: Promise it your house will not fall

effects.log: It cannot know whether you mean it. It comes anyway.
It seems to respect that more.

events.text: Outside the gate of the Secret Realm, as the barrier closes behind you, you unwrap your coat to look again. The egg is the size of a man's head, speckled like a river stone, and warm as a hearth brick. When you put your ear to it something inside knocks twice, very politely.

effects.log: You knock twice. After a long moment, it knocks twice again.

choices.text: Hide it from the other sects' parties

effects.log: You walk out past them with an ordinary face and an extraordinary coat.
The elders fall silent around it. One of them, very old, starts to cry and will not say why.

events.text: Behind the dead master's seat, in a nest of ash and old feathers, there is an egg. It should be stone after all these years. It is not. It is warm, and it turns very slightly toward your lantern, the way a sleeper turns toward a voice.

choices.text: Carry it out in your arms

effects.log: You climb out of the cave with the egg against your chest. Something in it is listening to your heart.

choices.text: Bow to the master's seat first

effects.log: You bow to the empty seat. Perhaps the master meant this as the true inheritance.

events.text: Old Bae Dol, who kept beasts for three houses before yours and has buried two of them, turns the egg over in his big scarred hands. "Straw, not silk," he says. "A brazier, not a fire. Talk to it. They hatch for a voice, not for heat."

effects.log: You build the nest his way. Bae Dol grunts, which from him is praise.

choices.text: Ask him about the houses he served

effects.log: "Two fell," he says. "Not because of their beasts." He does not say more.

events.text: The egg splits in the night with a sound like ice breaking on a river, and {gb_name} comes out of it all at once: wet, furious, much bigger than the egg should have held, and already trying to bite the straw. Old Bae Dol, who sat up with it, laughs until he has to sit down.

effects.log: {gb_name}, you call it, in front of the whole house. It bites your sleeve. The name holds.
It eats a week of meat in an hour and falls asleep in your lap. Your legs go numb. You do not move.

events.text: It hatches in fire. The straw catches, the nest catches, and out of the flames comes {gb_name}, a little thing of red and gold that shakes the sparks off its feathers like water and looks at you, offended that you have not yet applauded.

effects.log: You clap. It preens. The servants put out the barn.
It sulks for a day, then forgives you, then sets fire to your hat.

events.text: Nothing happens for a whole day after the shell cracks. Then a small, very ancient-looking head comes out, blinks at the lantern, and goes back in. {gb_name} is in no hurry. Old Bae Dol says the ones that take their time live the longest.

effects.log: By evening it has come all the way out and is asleep on your foot.

choices.text: Coax it out with a fish

effects.log: It considers the fish for an hour, and eats it with dignity.

events.text: On a clear night you look up at the mountains behind the house and feel, without any reason, that something up there is looking back. You know the shape of those slopes the way you know the shape of your own hand. You have never climbed them in this life.

choices.text: Ask Old Bae Dol about the old beacon on the peak

effects.log: "Your house lit it once, to call its guardian," he says. "Nobody has for a long time. Nobody had anything to call."

choices.text: Stand at the gate until the feeling passes

effects.log: It does not pass. It waits, like you.

events.text: In a dream you are not yourself. You are vast and slow and very old, and you are lying on a mountain looking down at a house with lanterns in its windows, wondering who lives there now. You wake with the dream's weight still in your limbs.

effects.log: You write it down. In the morning the ink has run, as if the page had been out in the rain.

choices.text: Go out and look at the mountain

effects.log: The mountain looks the same as always. You do not.

events.text: The beacon burns on the peak all night. Near dawn the snow on the high slopes shifts, and {gb_name} comes down through it, unhurried, as if returning from an errand. It stops before you and looks at you for a long time, and then it does something no beast has done for you in this life: it lays its head against your chest, like a greeting between old friends.

effects.log: You do not know what you remember. You know it is true.

choices.text: Laugh, and do not know why

effects.log: It makes a sound you have never heard a beast make. It is laughing too.

events.text: Old Bae Dol has kept beasts for three houses and has never been afraid of one. He is afraid of this one. "It knows the way to the courtyard," he says. "It walked straight to the old feeding trough. That trough was buried forty years ago."

effects.log: You dig it up together. {gb_name} watches the work with great approval.

choices.text: Tell him not to be afraid

effects.log: "I am not afraid of it," he says. "I am afraid of what it means about you."

events.text: The keepers bring you to the courtyard on your first morning as head of {gb_house}. {gb_name} is lying in the sun where it lay for your predecessor. It opens one eye, looks at you, and closes it again. It is not unkind. It has seen heads come and go, and it is waiting to see what kind you are.

choices.text: Sit down in the sun beside it

effects.log: You sit. After a while it shifts over to make room.

choices.text: Tell it the house is in good hands

effects.log: It opens both eyes this time. You had better be right.

choices.text: Ask the keepers what your predecessor fed it

effects.log: Yun Sori tells you everything, down to the hour. You write it down.

events.text: {gb_name} will not come out of its shelter for the new head of {gb_house}. It lies in the shadow at the back and watches you with an old, careful patience, the way it must have watched every head before you. Yun Sori, the keeper, says it grieves the last one. It will take time.

choices.text: Leave its favourite food at the entrance

effects.log: In the morning the food is gone. The shelter is still dark.

choices.text: Come every evening and read aloud

effects.log: You read the house's annals to the dark. On the ninth night, it comes to the doorway to listen.
It does not come out. The keepers look at their feet.

events.text: {gb_name} comes to meet the new head of {gb_house} at the gate, and stops three paces away. It looks at your hands, and then at your face, and then it turns its back and walks to the far end of the courtyard. The whole house sees it. Nobody says anything. Everybody knows what it means.

effects.log: You bear it. Some refusals are earned, and the earning goes both ways.
You rage. It does not turn around. The house hears that too.

choices.text: Ask Old Bae Dol what it saw

effects.log: "What you did," he says. "They always know. It is the only thing they are for."

events.text: The new head of {gb_house} walks into the courtyard, and {gb_name} gets up at once and comes across it, quickly, the way it came down the mountain once to the beacon. It sniffs your hands and your hair, and then it sits down against your legs so heavily you have to brace yourself. The keepers have never seen it do that.

choices.text: Kneel and put your arms around it

effects.log: It allows it. Its breathing goes slow and deep, as if a long errand were over.
It huffs, very softly. It means: you again.

events.text: One evening {gb_name} comes out of the far corner of the courtyard where it has kept itself all these months, and lies down a little closer to the hall than before. Not close. But closer. Something in you has changed, and it has seen it.

choices.text: Do not go to it yet

effects.log: You do not go to it. You sit on the hall steps where it can see you, and let it decide.
It does not look at you. Its tail moves, once.

events.text: The whole house gathers in the courtyard at dawn. {gb_name} walks a slow circle around you, three times, close enough that its breath stirs your sleeve, and then it stops before you and bows its great head to the ground. Old Bae Dol lets out a breath he must have been holding for a year.

effects.log: You bow lower than it did. The house sees that too, and will remember.

choices.text: Lay your hand on its head

effects.log: It is warm, and very still, and yours. You are its, too, now.

events.text: The trial is not what anyone tells you it will be. {gb_name} simply lies down across the gate of {gb_house} and refuses to let you out for a day and a night, to see what you do. You do not shout. You do not force it. You sit down on your side of it and wait, and at dawn it gets up and lets you through, and the keepers ring the bell.

effects.log: You walk through. Behind you, it falls in at your heel.
You sit until the sun is up. It lies back down beside you. Nobody is in a hurry now.

events.text: {gb_name} walks a slow circle around you before the whole house, three times. Then it stops, looks at you for a long, long moment, and walks away to its shelter without bowing. Yun Sori, the keeper, catches your eye and shakes her head very slightly: not no. Not yet.

effects.log: You go after it. It lets you sit at the entrance of its shelter, but no further.

choices.text: Let the house see you take it calmly

effects.log: You take it calmly. Some of the elders look at you a little differently, and not worse.

events.text: The trial ends with you on your back in the courtyard dust and {gb_name} standing over you, one great paw on your chest, not pressing. It looks at you, and lets you up, and goes. You were not afraid. You were not ready either. It knows the difference.

choices.text: Get up and brush yourself off

effects.log: You get up. Somebody in the crowd laughs. Next year nobody will.

choices.text: Ask the keeper what you did wrong

effects.log: "Nothing," Yun Sori says. "You just did not do it yet."

events.text: The beast-keeper Old Bae Dol has taken an apprentice: Yun Sori, a girl from the village with burn scars on both hands and no fear of anything with teeth. {gb_name} took to her in a day. Bae Dol pretends to be offended.

choices.text: Let her keep it in the winter months

effects.log: She keeps it beautifully. Your hands are free, and so, a little, is your heart.
"A kitchen fire," she says. "I went back in for the dog." {gb_name} seems to know the story already.

events.text: Years have passed. Yun Sori, who came to the courtyard as Old Bae Dol's apprentice, is the keeper of {gb_name} now. Bae Dol sits in the sun by the gate most days, telling anyone who will stop how he taught her everything she knows, and how she ignored half of it, and how that was the right half.

effects.log: He tells you about the houses he served before yours. Two fell. He is very sure this one will not.
She takes the old bronze seal in her scarred hands as if it were made of glass.

events.text: You spend a morning grooming {gb_name} in the courtyard of {gb_house}: burrs out of its coat, a cracked claw filed, a long talk about nothing. It pretends to tolerate you. It leans into the brush every time.

effects.log: It listens to everything and judges nothing, which is more than any elder does.
The silence is good. You both needed it.

events.text: Children of the house dare each other to touch {gb_name}'s tail while it sleeps. It is not asleep. It has never once been asleep when they try. It lets them, every time, and opens one eye afterwards so they know.

effects.log: You pretend. It pretends. The children are sure they are the bravest in the province.
They shriek and scatter. {gb_name} looks at you reproachfully. That was the fun part.

events.text: {gb_name} is still small enough to climb into your lap and too big to fit there. It tries anyway, every evening, and you end up underneath it in the courtyard, laughing, while the servants step carefully around you both.

effects.log: It wins. It always wins. That is the point.
It learns to sit. It sits on you.

events.text: {gb_name} is so old now that pilgrims come to {gb_house} just to look at it. It lies in the courtyard like a hill with eyes, and lets them. Once in a while it lifts its head and looks at one of them, and that one goes home and changes their whole life.

choices.text: Ask it which one it chose today

effects.log: It looks at the gate. A young porter is standing there, very pale. You hire the porter.

choices.text: Close the gate for a day of quiet

effects.log: You close the gate. It sleeps all day in the sun. So, for an hour, do you.

events.text: The White Tiger of the house has a habit of lying on the roof of the ancestral hall at dusk, where every village in the valley can see it. The tiles crack every winter. Nobody would dream of asking it to move.

effects.log: The roofer has stopped asking why.

choices.text: Climb up and sit with it

effects.log: From the roof you can see every lamp in the valley being lit. It was guarding all of them.

events.text: The Haechi of the house has started following the stewards around the treasury. It sits beside the ledger desk all day and stares. Two stewards have resigned. The accounts have never been so honest.

effects.log: By the end of the year the treasury is fuller than it has ever been.

choices.text: Ask it to leave the honest ones alone

effects.log: It looks at you as if the question were very foolish. It already does.

events.text: The fox of the house has borrowed a face again. This morning it was a visiting scholar who ate three bowls of rice and argued with the elders about poetry. The elders lost. The fox is very pleased with itself.

effects.log: It looks ashamed for exactly as long as you are watching.

choices.text: Ask it to argue with them again next week

effects.log: It accepts with a bow that has nine tails in it.

events.text: The iron-eater of the house has eaten the gate hinges again. The smiths have learned to forge a set of spare hinges every month, and to leave the scrap by its trough, and to never, ever leave their hammers lying around.

choices.text: Feed it the old armour in the store-room

effects.log: It eats a whole rusted suit and sleeps for three days, smiling.

choices.text: Let the smiths have their way

effects.log: The smiths build a cage of bronze, which it does not like the taste of. Everyone is unhappy.

events.text: You ride out through the province with {gb_name} pacing beside your horse. In every village people come out of their doors to watch the guardian of {gb_house} go by. An old woman holds up her grandchild to see. The child waves. {gb_name}, to everyone's astonishment, turns its head and looks back.

choices.text: Stop and let the child touch it

effects.log: The child pats its nose with great seriousness. The whole village will tell this story for fifty years.
You ride on. Behind you, the village is still talking.

events.text: {gb_name} has its own opinion about which road to take. Halfway up a goat track it stops, sits down, and will not go on. You go on. It was right. The track ends in a cliff, and you come home bruised and humbled while it trots along beside you looking very satisfied.

effects.log: It accepts the apology and steps on your foot.
It is a good laugh. Your ribs hurt.

events.text: When {gb_name} walks into a market town now, the town stops. Bandits on the high road have moved to another province. Magistrates who meant to cheat your tenants find, quite suddenly, that they had misread the law. A great beast keeps the peace better than any army, and it never has to draw.

effects.log: The magistrate is very glad to see you, and very glad to see you go.

choices.text: Buy every child in the market a sweet

effects.log: The children follow {gb_name} out of town like a festival.

events.text: {gb_name} is no longer a hatchling. You notice it one morning when it stands up in the courtyard and its shoulder is level with the well-head. Old Bae Dol measures it with a rope and grumbles that the shelter will have to be rebuilt.

choices.text: Rebuild it larger than it needs

effects.log: You build it for the beast it will be, not the one it is.

choices.text: Let it choose where to sleep

effects.log: It chooses your doorstep. That settles that.

events.text: {gb_name} is fully grown. Merchants passing through the province start to say "{gb_house}" instead of the house's own name, and then the jianghu does, and then one day your own steward writes it on a letter without noticing. The beast has become your house's symbol.

choices.text: Have the new name carved over the gate

effects.log: The carvers work for a month. {gb_name} supervises.

choices.text: Let the old name stand too

effects.log: Both names go over the gate, the old above the new. The house remembers what it was.

choices.text: Sew its image on the house's banner

effects.log: The new banner goes up. People bow to it in the street. Some of them bow to the beast.

events.text: {gb_name} has become a great beast, the kind that turns up in teahouse stories in provinces it has never visited. A sect from the far west sends a delegation with gifts just to look at it. It looks back at them until they leave.

effects.log: They leave the gifts and hurry home with a story.
They go home with nothing but the story, which is worth more to them.

events.text: {gb_name} is ancient now: older than the oldest stone in {gb_house}, older than its oldest grudge. When it walks the courtyard the ground seems to remember it. Yun Sori, grey-haired, says it no longer eats much. It mostly listens.

effects.log: You sit with it at dusk and listen. You hear the house breathing, every room of it.

choices.text: Write its life into the annals

effects.log: You write it all down, every head it served. The list is longer than you thought.

events.text: Raiders of {gb_foe} came over the hills at night to burn a granary of {gb_house}. They got as far as the stream. On the far bank, very still in the moonlight, {gb_name} was waiting for them. They went home. Nobody had to draw.

effects.log: You thank them for their visit. They do not write back.
It eats the feast. Then it eats the table.

events.text: An envoy of {gb_foe} comes to {gb_house} to talk about the old feud, and finds himself shown into a hall where {gb_name} is lying across the doorway. He has to step over it to reach his seat. He is very polite for the rest of the visit.

effects.log: His hands shake so badly he spills it. The feud cools a little more.

choices.text: Ask him to step over it again on the way out

effects.log: He does. It yawns as he passes. He will never forget that yawn.

events.text: In the sect war, {gb_name} goes out with the house's fighters to the gate. The other side breaks at the sight of it before the first charge. In the evening, while the wounded are carried in, it walks among them and lies down beside the worst, and stays until they sleep.

choices.text: Walk with it among the wounded

effects.log: You walk the rows with it. Nobody who sees it that night ever leaves the house.
The story goes out before you have washed the blood off. {gb_house} is feared now, and loved.

events.text: The sect war is lost. {gb_name} held the inner gate until the last of the house was through, and came back limping, its coat scorched and torn. It will heal. It lies in its shelter with its head on its paws and will not eat, as if it blames itself.

effects.log: You sit with it. Near dawn it eats from your hand.

choices.text: Tell it the house still stands

effects.log: It lifts its head at that. The house still stands. That was its whole work.

events.text: When {gb_name} came onto the field the enemy's banners wavered, and their fighters remembered sudden errands at home. The war is won. The teahouses already have a song about it, which is mostly wrong, and which {gb_name} seems to enjoy.

effects.log: You learn the song. You sing it badly. The house joins in.

choices.text: Have the true story written down

effects.log: The house's chronicler writes it plain. It is a better story true.

events.text: Yun Sori finds you in the hall. "It has stopped eating from anyone's hand but mine," she says, "and yesterday it would not eat from mine." {gb_name} has not seen the head of the house in years. It has noticed.

effects.log: You go. It does not get up, but it does not turn away.
She looks at you for a long moment, and says she will.

events.text: {gb_name} has taken to lying at the gate of {gb_house} with its face toward the mountains. It is not guarding the gate. It is looking at the road out. Old Bae Dol has seen a beast do this twice before, in the two houses that fell.

effects.log: "Be its head," he says. "Not its owner. It never belonged to anyone."
The gate is shut. It looks at the bars, and then at you.

events.text: They say {gb_name} came down on a farm in the night and broke the pens, and the farmers barred their doors and listened to it until dawn. It took nothing. It only wanted to be heard. Now there are hunters in the valley, and a price on the head of the beast that guarded your house.

choices.text: Pay the farmers for their pens

effects.log: You pay. They take it without meeting your eyes.
You call them off with silver and with threats. Most of them go home.

choices.text: Go up into the hills after it

effects.log: You go up. The hills are empty. Somewhere far off it hears you calling, and does not come.

events.text: In the morning the courtyard is empty. The straw is cold. A line of prints goes out of the gate, across the field and up the mountain without once turning back. Yun Sori sits in the empty shelter and will not come out.

effects.log: You sit with her in the cold straw. Neither of you says it was your fault. Both of you know.

choices.text: Follow the tracks to the treeline

effects.log: The tracks go into the pines and stop, as if it had simply stepped out of the world.

events.text: {gb_name} leaves at dawn, through the open gate, past the whole house gathered to watch. It stops once, on the rise, and looks back. Not at the house. At you. Then it goes. The guardian of the house would not stay with a head it could not honour.

effects.log: You bow. It is the first thing you have done in a long time that it would have liked.
You turn away first. The house sees that, too.

events.text: Rat-Ear Gu is the best thief in four provinces, and {gb_foe} paid him a fortune for one night's work. In the morning the courtyard of {gb_house} is empty, there are drugged meat-scraps in the straw, and a single grey thread is caught on the gate's iron, as if left there on purpose.

effects.log: You fold it into your sleeve. A thief who signs his work can be found.
Riders go out on every road before noon. The trail is already cold on most of them.
"Gu walks like a cat and drives a cart like a drunk," he says. "I will find the cart."

events.text: {gb_name} ate a deer carcass left at the edge of your lands and lay down in the field and did not get up. Nam Hwa, a physician of beasts, comes from two provinces away, looks into its eyes and smells its breath. "Dang Ilmae's work," she says. "I would know it anywhere. There is an antidote. It is not cheap, and it does not always take."

effects.log: "A few years, if it is strong," she says. "It is very strong."
"{gb_foe}, this time," she says. "Last time it was someone else. She does not care."

choices.text: Sit with it in the field

effects.log: You sit with it in the field until it is carried in. Its eyes follow you the whole way.

events.text: A thief came over the wall of {gb_house} in the night with a sack of drugged meat. {gb_name} was waiting for him on the other side. In the morning the keepers find him sitting very still in the middle of the courtyard, where it has kept him all night with one paw on his sash.

choices.text: Send him back to {gb_foe} with a message

effects.log: You send him home with a letter that says only: "It was awake."
He goes. He will never steal again. He cannot stop shaking.

events.text: A poisoned carcass is left at the edge of your lands. {gb_name} walks around it three times, looks toward the lands of {gb_foe}, and buries it, deep, with great care, so that nothing else will eat it either.

choices.text: Dig it up and have it examined

effects.log: Nam Hwa, the beast-physician, names the poison and the poisoner in one breath: Dang Ilmae.
You praise it. It ignores you magnificently.

events.text: You find {gb_name} three provinces away, chained in a barn behind a teahouse of ill repute, thinner and furious. When it sees you it goes quiet. When the chains come off it does not run. It walks out beside you as if it had only been waiting for you to finish your errand.

effects.log: You burn the barn. Nobody inside it protests. Nobody inside it stays.

choices.text: Leave the chains on the teahouse door

effects.log: You hang the chains on the teahouse door. It is the only message {gb_foe} will need.

events.text: The cart tracks lead to a ferry, and the ferry to a town where nobody has seen anything, and nobody will look you in the eye. Rat-Ear Gu's people were waiting. You get away with your life and a long cut, and the trail is colder.

choices.text: Bind the cut and keep going

effects.log: You keep going. Somewhere ahead, {gb_name} is waiting for you to be good enough.

choices.text: Go home and gather more help

effects.log: You go home. Next year, with Dosu and a dozen riders.

events.text: The trail of {gb_name} has gone cold for good. Dosu the tracker comes home with nothing for the first time in his life and sits at the gate with his head in his hands. Whoever has it now, it is not {gb_house}.

choices.text: Leave its shelter as it is

effects.log: You leave the straw and the trough. The keepers sweep it every day, out of habit and hope.
You swear it in the ancestral hall. The ancestors have heard such oaths before.

events.text: By the third night after the antidote, {gb_name} lifts its head off the straw and looks at you as if you had been gone a long time. Nam Hwa, the beast-physician, packs her needles and says the fever is broken. She refuses half her fee. "I have wanted to beat Dang Ilmae for twenty years," she says.

choices.text: Pay her the whole fee anyway

effects.log: She takes it, scowling, and leaves you a jar of salve for its paws.

choices.text: Feed it from your own hand

effects.log: It eats slowly from your hand. Its breath is clean.

events.text: The antidote does not take. {gb_name} sleeps and sleeps. Nam Hwa sits by it with her fingers on the great vein in its neck and says that it is strong, that there is still time, that she has one more idea. You can see that she is not sure of the idea.

effects.log: She stays. She sleeps in the straw beside it.
You sit up with it. Once in the night it opens its eyes, sees you, and closes them again, satisfied.

events.text: They carry {gb_name} home from the gate on a door, and lay it in the courtyard where it lay in the sun for so many years. Yun Sori kneels beside it. The whole house comes, one by one, and stands. Nobody tells the children to go inside. They stand with everyone else.

effects.log: You light the incense for a guardian of the house, as for one of the blood. The elders do not object. None of them.

choices.text: Have its name carved in the ancestral hall

effects.log: Its name goes into the hall beside the heads it served. It earned its place.
You sit with it until morning. Something in you will always be sitting there.

events.text: In the end the poison wins. {gb_name} dies in the night, quietly, with its head on your knee and Nam Hwa's hand on its neck. The physician weeps without a sound. In the morning a letter comes from {gb_foe}, asking after its health.

effects.log: You burn it unread. The ash goes up into a clear sky.
You write one line: "It died guarding the house." They will understand what that means for them.

choices.text: Bury it on the mountain it came from

effects.log: You carry it up the mountain yourself. It is very light, at the end.

events.text: When the plaque of the absorbed sect comes down, its guardian beast walks out of the empty hall and sits in the gateway, looking at its scattered people. Then it gets up and follows them into your house. It does not look at you. It is not following you. It is following them.

choices.text: Give it the absorbed sect's old hall

effects.log: You give it the hall it knew. It lies down in it, and some of its people stop weeping.
It comes. It does not lie down for a week.

events.text: The absorbed sect's guardian beast will not stay under your banner. It breaks out through the back wall the night the plaque comes down and goes into the hills, and its old disciples watch it go with a look you will remember the next time you think of swallowing a sect.

effects.log: You let it go. It owes you nothing. It is the only one of them who knows it.
The hunters come home empty-handed and frightened. The disciples smile at their feet.

events.text: The absorbed sect's guardian comes to your gate, meets {gb_name} in the courtyard, and the two great beasts look at each other for a long time. Then the newcomer turns and goes into the hills. There is not room in one house for two guardians, and both of them knew it before you did.

effects.log: You watch it out of sight. {gb_name} watches with you.
It looks at you as if to say: it was never a question.

events.text: News comes from the steppe: {gb_empire} has fallen, and {gb_ebeast} did not follow the new khans. She ran south with no banner beside her, and herders hear her howling at night from hills that have no name. A guardian with no empire is a dangerous, lonely thing.

effects.log: Once, on the north wind, you think you hear her. It is the loneliest sound in the world.

choices.text: Send word to the border garrisons

effects.log: You warn the garrisons not to hunt her. Some of them listen.

events.text: {gb_empire} has fallen, and {gb_ebeast} has left the delta. The ferrymen say the rivers ran backwards for a whole day when she went. Now she swims where she likes, and the river towns of the south tie rice cakes to every prow and pray she does not like theirs.

choices.text: Tie a rice cake to a prow yourself

effects.log: You tie it on. The ferryman thanks you. You are not sure why you did it.

choices.text: Ask where she was last seen

effects.log: Upriver, they say. Toward the ten provinces. Toward you.

events.text: With {gb_empire} fallen, {gb_ebeast} no longer guards its harbour castles. The fishing fleets of the east coast say it has coiled itself around an island that was not there last year, and the sea for a day's sail around is calm as glass, and nobody will sail on it.

choices.text: Ask a captain to take you near

effects.log: No captain will. One offers to sell you a boat instead.

choices.text: Write it in your own journal

effects.log: You write it down: the day the sea dragon became nobody's.

events.text: {gb_empire} has fallen, and {gb_ebeast} has come down from the plateau alone. It walks the old caravan roads like a pilgrim, and lies down outside monastery gates, and the monks bring it butter lamps and do not know what else to do.

choices.text: Send the monastery a gift of butter

effects.log: You send butter for the lamps. The abbot writes back: it seems to like the light.

choices.text: Think about what it is waiting for

effects.log: An empire to guard, perhaps. Or a house.

events.text: The dynasty on the Dragon Throne has fallen. On the night the capital burned, {gb_ebeast} rose from the Dragon Altar and did not come down. Now the new house sits on the throne without it, and the provinces whisper that the Mandate has gone up into the clouds and might come down anywhere.

effects.log: The clouds over the capital are gold at the edges, for a long time after sunset.
Wise. Every ambitious house in the ten provinces is looking up.

events.text: {gb_empire} has fallen, and its guardian, {gb_ebeast}, is simply gone. Nobody saw it go. The temples say it went into the earth with the old house, to sleep until another house is worth guarding. The scholars say there was never any beast at all. The temples are fuller than the schools this year.

effects.log: You light incense for a beast you never saw. It feels right.
You side with the scholars at dinner. That night you dream of scales.

events.text: {gb_empire} has fallen, but its guardian, {gb_ebeast}, did not leave. On the first morning of the new house it came to the new ruler's gate and lay down there, and the new ruler went out and bowed to it before the whole court. A beast chooses a house, not a name.

effects.log: A beast chooses a house, not a name. You think on that for a long time.
You toast it. It may need the luck.

events.text: The hill where Gray Mother Ashina howls is bare and cold and very high. She comes down to meet you halfway, slowly, head low, the way wolves come to see what a stranger is. She is the size of a horse. She smells of snow and old smoke.

choices.text: Stand and let it look at you

effects.log: You stand. It looks. Whatever it sees, it does not leave.

choices.text: Speak to it of your house

effects.log: You speak of your house: its people, its gate, its long years. It listens to all of it.

choices.text: Draw your weapon, slowly, and lay it down

effects.log: You lay it down in the snow between you. It looks at the blade, and at you, and comes a step closer.

events.text: You wait on the riverbank at dawn while the water slows and stops and turns. Nine-Coil Nammae lifts her head out of the river, as tall as a watchtower, and looks down at you with eyes like two drowned moons.

choices.text: Stand and let it look at you

effects.log: You stand. It looks. Whatever it sees, it does not leave.

choices.text: Speak to it of your house

effects.log: You speak of your house: its people, its gate, its long years. It listens to all of it.

choices.text: Draw your weapon, slowly, and lay it down

effects.log: You lay it down in the snow between you. It looks at the blade, and at you, and comes a step closer.

events.text: The boat you bought drifts up to the new island on a sea as flat as a mirror. The island opens one eye. Old Shiokaze has been waiting a long time for someone foolish enough to come this close.

choices.text: Stand and let it look at you

effects.log: You stand. It looks. Whatever it sees, it does not leave.

choices.text: Speak to it of your house

effects.log: You speak of your house: its people, its gate, its long years. It listens to all of it.

choices.text: Draw your weapon, slowly, and lay it down

effects.log: You lay it down in the snow between you. It looks at the blade, and at you, and comes a step closer.

events.text: At the monastery gate the monks step aside for you without a word. Gangkar the White lifts its maned head from the snow and looks at you, and the butter lamps along the wall all lean the same way, as if in a wind.

choices.text: Stand and let it look at you

effects.log: You stand. It looks. Whatever it sees, it does not leave.

choices.text: Speak to it of your house

effects.log: You speak of your house: its people, its gate, its long years. It listens to all of it.

choices.text: Draw your weapon, slowly, and lay it down

effects.log: You lay it down in the snow between you. It looks at the blade, and at you, and comes a step closer.

events.text: Eunuch Seo Gwan, Keeper of the Dragon Altar, has served four emperors and outlived three of them. He kneels before you with a single golden scale on a silk cushion. "The Yellow Dragon does not serve the throne," he says. "It serves the Mandate. When it stops coming to the altar, Majesty, the Mandate has already gone."

effects.log: "The rite," he says, "every year. And a reign it can stand to look at."

choices.text: Ask whether it came for the last emperor

effects.log: He does not answer for a long time. "Not at the end," he says.

choices.text: Take the scale in your own hand

effects.log: It is warm. It is very warm.

events.text: The rite at the Dragon Altar runs from midnight to dawn: drums, incense, the long litany in a language older than the empire. At first light the golden clouds over the altar part, and the Yellow Dragon looks down at you for the space of a breath, and is gone. Ha Ryun, the court astrologer, writes in his book: "It came."

choices.text: Ask Ha Ryun what he saw in its face

effects.log: "Patience, Majesty," he says. "For now."
You bow until the drums stop. The court sees an emperor who knows what the throne owes.

events.text: The Yellow Dragon has not come to the altar all year. Ha Ryun, the court astrologer, brings you his star charts with trembling hands. The ministers are counting the provinces that have stopped sending their full tax. Nobody says the word Mandate in your hearing. Everybody says it in the corridors.

effects.log: You order it. The treasury groans. The court watches the clouds.

choices.text: Ask Seo Gwan what it wants

effects.log: "A reign it can bear to look at, Majesty," he says, not quite meeting your eyes.
You silence them. The whispering moves to the provinces.

events.text: The Yellow Dragon comes to the altar now even when there is no rite. It coils on the palace roof in the evening sun and the whole capital stops to look up. Ha Ryun says he has never seen it so often in any reign he has read of. The Mandate has never sat so easily.

effects.log: You climb up. It lets you sit beside it. Below you, the capital is lighting its lamps.
You proclaim three days of feasting. The dragon watches the lanterns all three nights.

events.text: The Yellow Dragon is gone. Seo Gwan found the altar cold at dawn, and the golden scales that had lain on it for three hundred years turned to plain brass. He brings you one in his old hands. He does not say anything. He does not need to.

effects.log: You keep it on your desk, where you will see it every day.

choices.text: Ask him whether it can come back

effects.log: "Once," he says, "in the third reign of the old house. A great rite. A changed heart."
You throw it in the river. The court hears that you did.

events.text: At the end of the third night of the great rite, as the last drum stops, the Yellow Dragon comes down to the altar out of a clear sky and lies there in the dawn, looking at you. The scales on the altar are gold again. Old Seo Gwan sits down on the steps and weeps like a child.

effects.log: You sit beside him on the altar steps. The dragon watches you both.
You bow. It is a long bow. The court will talk of it for a generation.

events.text: Passing through a valley you have never visited, you see an old banner over a great gate: {gb_house}. In the courtyard, through the open gate, {gb_name} lifts its head from the sun and looks at you, a stranger on the road, for much longer than it looks at anyone else.

effects.log: You stop. It gets up and comes as far as the gate, and no further. It is not yours in this life. It knows you anyway.
You walk on. It watches you all the way down the valley.

events.text: A merchant from the east tells a story at an inn about {gb_house} and its guardian, {gb_name}, who has outlived more heads than anyone can count. You know the end of the story before he tells it. You do not know how.

effects.log: You tell him. He stares at you. "Nobody knows that part," he says.
He tells it again. You listen as if hearing about family.

events.text: At a temple fair a child is selling paper beasts, folded out of red paper, one for every great beast of the old stories. You buy one without thinking. On the way home you realise your eyes are wet, and you do not know which beast it was you were thinking of, only that it died for a house you loved.

effects.log: You keep it on the windowsill. It is the only thing in the room that never gathers dust.
You burn it at the shrine. The smoke goes up straight, as if something received it.

events.text: In the mountains a hunter tells you about a beast that has haunted the high valley for longer than his grandfather can remember: it guarded a house once, they say, and the house forgot it. When you go up to look, nothing is there. But on the way down you are sure, quite sure, that something is following you at a distance, and that it is sorry too.

effects.log: Nothing answers. The silence that comes back is not empty.

choices.text: Leave food on a flat rock

effects.log: In the morning the food is gone. Nothing else is.
